### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **35** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `83426b7b126c7371c05408aa1d6c3b6ee3ff0564` — the merge of head `cfce553f641ece82053a0eb1997a8958accecdd2` into base `27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 83426b7b126c7371c05408aa1d6c3b6ee3ff0564 && git checkout 83426b7b126c7371c05408aa1d6c3b6ee3ff0564
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a cfce553f641ece82053a0eb1997a8958accecdd2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a && git merge --no-ff cfce553f641ece82053a0eb1997a8958accecdd2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 27895d7ff60b64b30e48cbecdc35889b50c3096a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对
ACCEPT — PR #36620 @ `cfce553f641ece82053a0eb1997a8958accecdd2` · card #35384 (remainder: item 1 and the approval step label) · L1 by the seat's card thread · 2026-11-23T04:54Z

- Shape (`l1-face --pr 36620`): draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #35384`. `Fixes` is right: items 2–3 landed in PR #36598, item 1 of #36464, and this PR carries the last two (release 7082136476, partial landing 7090254542). No other card is bound. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` · `Metadata-protocol: none`; `Skills-docs:` not owed, present as `none`. One changeset covers all three published packages. Checks at this head (`pr-state`): 60 success · 13 expected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending; mergeable clean. The three reds on the earlier head 0b91c34b are `cancelled` (superseded by this push): no action.
- Diff read: spec adds `resolveFlowApprovalStepLabel(bundle, flowName, nodeId, literal?, opts?)` beside `resolveFlowScreenTitle`. It walks `localeChain(opts)` over `flows.<flow>.approvals.<node_id>.label`, own keys only, and answers `literal` on a miss. `translateFlow` is untouched. `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` move by one line each. The `flows.approvals.*.label` liveness evidence now cites the resolver. service-messaging accepts `{ object, fallback }` (`NotificationObjectLabelParam`, re-exported): a closed member set, and the API name checked against one catalog-key segment. A mixed `{ object, key }` shape is refused. `renderWith` resolves it with `translateObject` over `getSchema(name)` and `registry.getPackagedObjectBase(name)` off the data engine, with the `/meta` options (negotiated locale, declared fallback, `sourceLocale` else `defaultLocale`), built once per render and throw-safe, falling back to `fallback`. `{ key, fallback }` still goes through `t()`, so stored rows render as before. plugin-approvals `subjectParams` emits the typed param and `stepLabel` calls the spec resolver; `t()` now carries catalog sentences only.
- Seat rulings applied: option A (a spec export, not a copied locale chain). Naming 7091274184: the member is `object`, the type `NotificationObjectLabelParam`, the export `resolveFlowApprovalStepLabel`. The premise reading that ruled out a `translateFlow` overlay is in the PR body: the read points hold only `process_name` and `current_step`.
- Tests: the service-messaging and plugin-approvals integration tests run on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`. The spec resolver has its own cases (locale chain, authored locale, literal fallback, empty bundle, prototype keys). Five-leg ablation in the os-dev-report: 1a 5/7, 1b 1/7, 2 5/37, 3 1/5, 4 2/8 red, each restored to the HEAD blob; the rename round changes no behaviour. Suites: service-messaging 80 files / 1084, plugin-approvals 127 / 1883, spec 880 / 28058. Typecheck exit 0 across the three packages. 97/97 gate families exit 0 at this head (`35384-item1-gates-ran-r2.txt`, 0 NOT-MEASURED).
- Changeset read sentence by sentence: patch for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-messaging` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`. The three bullets match the diff, and so does the closing upgrade-together line: an older messaging service refuses `{ object }` at `emit()`.
- Accepted deviations: a `t()`-only i18n service (no `getTranslations`) gets the param's `fallback` (the #36464 precedent; `getTranslations` is a required `II18nService` member). Patch-level changesets under `Metadata-protocol: none`. The worktree was pushed from a local branch name, because the shared checkout holds the thread branch.
- Out of scope: none filed; no ADR sentence to carry (0 hits in `docs/adr`). Security: none. #36467 (one options builder) is not folded in; this PR adds one more inline copy of the options, in service-messaging, and that card's census should count it.
- Owed: an L2 contract review (`Clause-②: yes`: a new spec export and a widened service-messaging accept set), requested from l2-review#4 at this head. Landing goes to the seat; this thread does not land.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cfce553f641ece82053a0eb1997a8958accecdd2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/services/service-messaging/src/notification-text.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-notification-text.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/reader-locale-labels.ts

PR #36620 (card #35384), net diff against merge base `c6075a78`, 14 files. Read: the card body and all 16 comments, the PR body and its 4 comments, the net diff of the five scope files plus the changeset and the three spec baselines, and the check-runs on this head (73 runs: 60 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending; Test Core, Test UI, Build Core, Lint and Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check UI, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard all success). Tests, the three generated baselines and the changeset prose are the lane's ACCEPT; the changeset is read for ② only.

### ① Derived judgments

- New spec export `resolveFlowApprovalStepLabel(bundle, flowName, nodeId, literal?, opts?)` from `@objectstack/spec/system`: a public-surface widening, additive. `api-surface/system.json` and `export-origins/system.json` each gain exactly that one row. Right.
- `translateFlow`, `translateObject`, `ResolveOptions`, `localeChain` and `pickData` are untouched; no existing spec export changes meaning. Right.
- service-messaging accept set: `NotificationTextKeys.params` values widen from `string | { key, fallback }` to also `{ object, fallback }`. `problemOf` admits the new arm with a closed member set and refuses `{ object, fallback, key }`, a non-string `fallback`, and an `object` that is not one identifier segment. The `{ key, fallback }` arm is byte-for-byte the same judgement as on main. Widening only. Right.
- `OBJECT_NAME_SHAPE` (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`) against real object API names: `ObjectSchema.name` on this head is `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$` (`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts:4056`), a strict subset, so no authorable object name is refused. An object name carries no dot, so nothing the old `objects.NAME.label` key could spell is lost. Right.
- service-messaging exported types: `NotificationObjectLabelParam` is newly exported from the package index, `NotificationTextParam` gains a union arm, and `NotificationTextI18n` gains four optional members (`getTranslations`, `getFallbackLocale`, `getSourceLocale`, `getDefaultLocale`). All additive; the optional members are not named in the changeset, which is acceptable for optional structural members a real `II18nService` already has. Right.
- Stored-row compatibility, both directions. A row written by this head with `{ object, fallback }` and read by an older `readNotificationTextKeys`: the older `problemOf` reports an undeclared member, the reader returns no keys, and the stored literal is delivered (graceful). A row written by an older emitter with `{ key, fallback }` and read by this head: unchanged `t()` path. Right.
- Version skew: a new plugin-approvals over an older messaging service is refused at `emit()`; `ApprovalService.notify` catches and warns (`approval-service.ts` near 2586), so an approval never fails, the notification is lost. All three packages are in the one changeset `fixed` group (`.changeset/config.json`), so they version together, and the changeset states the upgrade-together rule. Right.
- plugin-approvals: `ApprovalTextParam`, `ApprovalObjectLabelParam` and `ApprovalSubjectParams` are module-level types not re-exported from the package index and have no consumer outside the package (git grep over packages, ui, examples). No published surface moves there. Right.
- Liveness row `flows.approvals.label` re-anchors its evidence on the spec resolver; the gate `Spec property liveness` is success on this head.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — present line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, with `Metadata-protocol: none` beside it in both. Confirmed against the diff: one new spec export and one widened service-messaging accept set, no narrowing arm anywhere.

`Metadata-protocol: none` holds: nothing a metadata author can write changes. The translation key `flows.FLOW.approvals.NODE_ID.label` was already declared in `translation.zod.ts`; the notification param is a runtime producer contract, not authored metadata. Under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3 the kind `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The changeset carries `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-messaging` and `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, the three packages the diff moves. `Check Changeset` is success on this head. The level is right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation, export choice: seat ruling 7090334812 preferred an overlay inside `translateFlow`, conditional on the read point holding the flow document. Verified in the tree: `localizeRequestLabels` reads only `process_name` and `current_step` off the row, and `flowLabel` hands `translateFlow` a name-only stub. The premise fails as the dev measured, and seat ruling 7091274184 item 1 accepts `resolveFlowApprovalStepLabel`. Answered.
- Seat ruling 7091274184 item 2, member `object`, type `NotificationObjectLabelParam`: applied. No stale `objectLabel` spelling of the param remains in shipped code, docblocks, validator messages, tests under `service-messaging/src`, or the changeset. The remaining hits are the renderer's private method `objectLabel(...)` and the `subjectParams(objectName, objectLabel, record)` parameter, which does hold a label. Answered.
- Dev deviation, patch not minor: right, see ②.
- Dev deviation, a `t()`-only i18n double receives the param's `fallback`: accepted. `II18nService.getTranslations` and `getLocales` are required members of the contract, and the fallback is the schema label the producer already holds.
- Dev deviation, forced test edits and the worktree branch name: lane matters, no contract effect.
- `open_questions`: none in the two reports on this PR. Earlier ones are carried by #36466 (landed: `/meta` now negotiates the request locale, read on main) and #36467 (one options builder; this PR adds one more inlined copy in service-messaging, already noted for that card's census by the L1 comment).
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no new query, id materialisation or in-app join. The object-label path reads the in-memory registry (`getSchema` is `registry.getObject`; `registry.getPackagedObjectBase`) and the i18n service's in-memory maps; the only database read on the render path is the existing one `sys_user` locale read per recipient. No N+1 against a store. Nothing to flag.
- Security: the label of an object was already carried to every recipient as the param's fallback and through `t()`; resolving it through the registry exposes nothing new. No finding.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` (hits), against seat rulings 7090334812 and 7091274184 and its first consumer `reader-locale-labels.ts`:
- Key shape `flows[flowName].approvals[nodeId].label` matches `translation.zod.ts` (the `approvals` group, addressed by `FlowNode.id` at any depth), the lint rung in `validate-translation-references.ts` (approval node ids, any depth) and the UI reader `ui/packages/i18n/src/flowLabels.ts`.
- Locale chain is `localeChain(opts)` through `pickData`, the same pair `lookupFlowLabel` and `lookupFlowScreenCopy` use: requested locale, then the declared chain, skipped when the requested locale is the authored one. The docblock says exactly this.
- Own-key guard on the node id is real (`hasOwnProperty` on the `approvals` map); a flow name such as `constructor` reaches a function whose `approvals` is undefined and is skipped. An empty-string entry is skipped and the walk continues, as the sibling lookups do. `literal` (here none) answers a miss.
- Row shape verified: `openNodeRequest` stores `current_step: input.nodeId` and snapshots the node label as `current_step_label`; `flowNameOfProcess` strips the `flow:` prefix. Node ids are unique across a flow at every depth (`flow.zod.ts` refuses a duplicate id by location), so a region's approval node cannot collide.
- The docblock's reason for not folding into `translateFlow` agrees with `translateFlow`'s own docblock (the node `label` is not overlaid).

`packages/services/service-messaging/src/notification-text.ts`, sentence by sentence against "resolved as GET /meta/object/:name serves it" (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts` on main):
- Options: `metaLabelTranslation` builds the bundle as `translationBundleOf` does and the options as `metaTranslateOptions` does (negotiated locale via `resolveBundleLocale` over `getLocales()`, `[getFallbackLocale()]`, `getSourceLocale()` else `getDefaultLocale()`). Since #36466 the meta door negotiates the same way, so an `en-US` recipient and an `en-US` request agree.
- Packaged base: `registry.getPackagedObjectBase(name)` is the body the protocol accessor reads (`protocol-discovery-and-bases.ts:851`).
- Pair bundle: none is passed, and none is owed. `servedOverrideBaseOf` answers `undefined` for type `object` (extended, never replaced, ADR-0146 D10; table in `served-override.ts`), so the meta door hands the object translator no `pairBundle` either. `patchBundles` feed field slots only and cannot move the object label.
- Label rule: `translateObject` decides `label` from `doc.label`, `packagedBase.label`, the bundle and the options alone, so the `{ name, label }` stub is sufficient input for the label.
- Served definition: `getSchema` is `registry.getObject`, the fold `/meta` serves for a code extension's rename, and stored object rows are registered into the same registry at hydration. This is the same source `reader-locale-labels.ts` reads since #36598.
- Throw safety: every read is wrapped; a failure yields the param's `fallback`, never a lost delivery. The validator and the renderer agree on the discriminant (`'object' in param`).

`packages/services/service-messaging/src/index.ts`: one type re-export, matching the changeset.

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-notification-text.ts`: `subjectParams` emits `{ object: objectName, fallback }`; `interpolate` still renders the literal from `fallback` for every non-string param, so the stored literal text is unchanged. The docblock agrees with the code.

`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/reader-locale-labels.ts`: `stepLabel` resolves through the spec resolver with the options already built once per read, memoised per flow and node; no flow document is read per row, and `attachFlowSteps` shares the same pick. `t()` now carries catalog sentences only, as the module docblock says.

N1 (nit) — The changeset calls the new export "the one reading of" the key, while `ui/packages/i18n/src/flowLabels.ts` (outside the diff) still reads `bundle[language].flows[flow].approvals[id].label` directly, with no locale chain. The spec docblock and the plugin docblock say "the spec's one reading", which is accurate. Left as a follow-up: the UI reader could adopt the resolver; no effect on this PR's contract.

N2 (nit) — `renderWith` builds the locale bundle once per rendered item, so a digest of M items for one recipient builds it M times (in-memory map reads only, no store read). The docblock's "once" is per render, which is what the code does. Left as an accepted deviation; hoisting to `renderAllFor` can ride #36467.

N3 (nit) — `packagedBaseOf` in messaging has no `getPackagedObjectOwner(name)?.definition` fallback for a registry that predates `getPackagedObjectBase`, which the protocol accessor keeps. It answers "no baseline known" there, the same as the approvals reader merged in #36598. Left as an accepted deviation.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [45115439638](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/45115439638) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test UI (13/16)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/45115439638/job/137498820589)** — 失败步骤: Run the ui tests (shard 13/16)

  ```

  × "Show me" reopens the action with its text, and fixing it there releases the hold 4074ms
  FAIL   dom  packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/DataPillar.panelHold-27629.test.tsx > DataPillar — an action predicate that does not parse holds with the draft (objectstack#27629) > leaving the
    ↳ 失败原因: AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
  FAIL   dom  packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/DataPillar.panelHold-27629.test.tsx > DataPillar — an action predicate that does not parse holds with the draft (objectstack#27629) > "Show me" r
    ↳ 失败原因: (这条 FAIL 之后 12 行内没有可识别的原因行 —— 点进 job 看)
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
